note: family-architecture.md §5.0a. A declared divergence is a DEBT, not a verdict: DIVERGE stays zero. Counted in §9.0 as a third quantity, never folded into coverage or gaps. Each row is gated in BOTH directions by the guards named in `gated_by` - one pinning that the model is STILL divergent (a silent fix leaves a stale declaration) and one pinning that the divergence has not WIDENED.

rows.site: LeanModels/Es/Eval.lean `instantiateFunction` - the `[[ThisMode]]` given to every non-arrow FunctionDeclaration/FunctionExpression. Observable as `this` inside a bare call in non-strict code.
rows.oracle: In non-strict code `[[ThisMode]]` is `global`, so OrdinaryCallBindThis (§10.2.1.2 steps 6.a-6.c) replaces an `undefined`/`null` thisArgument with the global object: `function f(){ return this }; f()` answers globalThis.
rows.model: Every function is created with `[[Strict]] = true` and `[[ThisMode]] = strict`, because the Directive Prologue (§11.2.2) is not read. §10.2.1.2 step 5 then binds the argument exactly as given, so the same call answers `undefined`.
rows.retirement_condition: The Directive Prologue (§11.2.2) is parsed and `[[ThisMode]]` becomes `global` for non-strict code. At that point the `.global` arm already present in `ordinaryCallBindThis` becomes REACHABLE and this silent difference turns into a loud refusal (`refuseHost`, 'needs the realm'), which is a boundary rather than a debt. Tracked as 2026-08-23-es-2.
rows.why_not_a_refusal: The refusal machinery for sloppy `this` EXISTS and is correct; it is simply unreachable, because no code path ever selects `.global`. An unreachable refusal is not a boundary - the model answers, and answers differently from the language, silently. That is what makes this a declared divergence and not a gap.
